neighbours.label: function words inside physical-science explanations of atoms, charge and energy
fire: Most of the mass of an atom is concentrated in its tiny, dense nucleus.
Inner electrons shield the outer electrons from the positive charge of the nucleus.
In a hydrogen atom the single electron is bound to the proton by electrostatic attraction.
The kinetic energy of a moving body is equal to one half of its mass times velocity squared.
Within a given shell, the energy of an orbital depends on the angular momentum quantum number.
Isotopes of an element differ in the number of neutrons found in the nucleus.
When an electron drops to a lower orbit, the atom emits a photon of definite energy.
Protons and neutrons are held together in the nucleus by the strong nuclear force.
quiet: Most of the money of the company is concentrated in its small head office downtown.
Tall hedges shield the back garden from the noise of the busy road.
In a small village the single shop is run by the same family for decades.
The price of a train ticket depends on the distance travelled and the time of day.
Within a given school, the size of a class depends on the year group.
Members of a choir differ in the range of notes they can comfortably sing.
When the bell rings, the children leave the room and walk to the hall.
Friends and neighbours are held together in the town by shared traditions.
